A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same uncertainty-estimation study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite section reorganization and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on IFEval and the Controlled/Realistic benchmarks, including AUROC scores, probing experiments and analyses of response length and task quality.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the benchmark comparisons and layer-wise probing results.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, uncertainty estimators and linear probing remain unchanged. The probing procedure moves from v1 Section 4 into v4 Section 2.1; its layers, optimizer and training parameters are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate IFEval and the same Controlled-Easy, Controlled-Hard and Realistic settings. The new IFEval examples in v4 Appendix A.5 illustrate existing coverage rather than introduce additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The six uncertainty estimators in the IFEval comparisons and the Probe-inclusive comparisons in Table 4 are unchanged. Moving the probing description into Section 2.1 does not add a comparator to the reported IFEval results.

E3.justification: The evaluated models, greedy decoding, AUROC metric, task-quality filtering and dataset counts are retained. Probe training still uses a 70/30 split and 1000 epochs. Histogram normalization changes the displays, not the experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The length-bias, task-quality, error-severity, instruction-type and probe-layer analyses already appear in v1. v4 redisplays existing distributions and adds illustrative input examples, without adding ablations, robustness tests or empirical case analyses.

E5.justification: Existing mean-and-standard-deviation summaries are retained, including Table 2 and v1 Table 10/v4 Table 11. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched performance tables, sample counts and length statistics retain their values. For example, LLaMA2-13B Probe AUROC remains 0.79, 0.58 and 0.64 across the three Table 4 settings. Normalized histograms re-express existing distributions rather than report new experimental findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical expressions defining the uncertainty scores are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs or formal derivations; the new dataset rationale is explanatory prose.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: systematic evaluation, the Controlled/Realistic benchmark design, benefits of self-evaluation and internal representations, and difficulty detecting subtle instruction violations.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.4 explicitly frames the intended scope as simple, unambiguous instructions and explains how complex prompts and LLM-based judges can confound uncertainty evaluation. It also discusses extending the benchmark-design considerations to future datasets. Existing result interpretations and conclusion limitations remain.

D1.justification: The first-page footnote changes from a future code/data release promise to reported availability with a repository address. Appendix A.3 also adds a brief input-only prompt box; existing substantive prompts and probe hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion remain unchanged. Moving Related Work from Section 5 to Section 4 and relocating the probing citation do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 integrates the standalone probing section into Methods and Results, grouping method comparisons by benchmark difficulty. It adds two explanatory appendix subsections and acknowledgments, and updates author information. Most prose and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2, 3 and 10 redraw length histograms using per-class proportions, with updated labels and captions. v4 adds illustrative Table 6, compacts the author block and redistributes existing appendix material; the remaining result displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v4 improves documented access through a code/data address and makes length-distribution comparisons clearer through class-normalized plots. The added IFEval rationale and examples help explain the evaluation design. These are useful, limited gains in clarity and reproducibility documentation; the empirical evidence and core limitations remain unchanged.
